To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we developed a method for targeted integration in Drosophia cell lines, and we demonstrated the utility of this method for improving the performance of cell-based assays.

we have developed a method for targeted integration into Drosophila S2 and Kc167 cell lines, and that this method can be used to create cell lines that express transgenes with high inducibility, low basal levels of expression, and high uniformity.

we developed an adaptation of φ C31 integrase– mediated targeted cassette exchange for the Drosophila S2 cell line and that the technology can be used to generate lines that have uniform and inducible expression of a gene of interest.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development and application of targeted genome engineering in Drosophia cell lines.
the development of new tools to facilitate targeted gene insertion into the genomes of Drosophila cells.
the development of new tools for the study of gene expression.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
targeted insertion is a valuable and powerful tool that can be used to improve Drosophila S2 cell-based assays.
the technology described here will allow researchers to perform targeted gene insertion into Drosophila cells.
this technology will greatly enhance the ability of the fly cell biology community to study the expression of transgenes in a variety of cell types.

the use of targeted cassette exchange allows for more uniform and more controlled gene expression in DrosophILA cells.
we have adapted the φC31 integrative system to Drosophila S2 cells and that we have demonstrated the utility of the system in the context of cell-based assays.
